headline: Anthropic may ask Claude users to upload government IDs for age verification
summary: The AI company is updating its privacy policy to require users to scan passports or driver's licenses, along with a selfie, for age and identity checks.
details: Anthropic is updating its privacy policy to include a requirement for users to verify their age and identity by uploading government-issued documents. This change, set to take effect on July 8, aims to allow users to appeal account flags for potentially fraudulent activity.

When triggered, the policy will require users to submit a scan of their passport or driver's license, along with a selfie and a digitized version for a face geometry template. Anthropic states this is to comply with various state and country regulations requiring age verification.

The company claims this measure is for a "small subset of users" whose accounts are flagged, not for general users. It is presented as an update to the appeals process and is unrelated to recent model rollouts.
Anthropic uses Persona, a San Francisco-based identity checking provider, for these verification processes. Persona is backed by Peter Thiel's Founder's Fund, which also invests in Anthropic.

This move comes amid ongoing scrutiny and pressure from the Trump administration, which has previously designated Anthropic a "supply chain risk" and clashed with the company over access to its AI tools.

headline_marked: Valve's Steam Machine [[launches today]] starting at $1,049
headline: Valve's Steam Machine launches today starting at $1,049
summary: Reservations are now open for Valve's Steam Machine, with the base 512GB model priced at $1,049 and a 2TB option available for $1,349.
details: After years of anticipation, Valve has officially opened reservations for the Steam Machine. The gaming console starts at $1,049 for a 512GB storage configuration, with a 2TB version priced at $1,349. These prices do not include the new Steam Controller, which adds $99 to the total cost, though a bundle offers a slight discount.

To ensure fair distribution and combat scalpers, Valve is implementing a lottery system for the initial batch. Only users with a Steam account in good standing who have made a purchase before April 27 are eligible to sign up. The reservation window closes on June 25, after which participants will be randomly assigned to a reservation or waitlist.

Those who secure a reservation will receive purchase emails starting June 29. Valve aims to avoid the chaotic rush of previous launches by extending the signup period, allowing for better validation and reducing the advantage of bots or those with rapid reaction times.

The Steam Machine features a semi-custom AMD Zen 4 6C/12T CPU and an AMD RDNA3 GPU, paired with 16GB of DDR5 RAM and 8GB of GDDR6 VRAM. It includes a microSD card slot for expandable storage, making it easy to transfer game files between the Steam Machine and Steam Deck.

Connectivity options include two USB 2.0 ports, two USB 3.2 Gen 1 ports, and a USB-C port. Display outputs are handled by DisplayPort 1.4 and HDMI 2.0. The system also supports Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3, with an integrated 2.4GHz adapter for the Steam Controller. The compact cube measures approximately six inches on each side.
